properties.decision: What the reader sees: an objection aimed at a step (its warrant) that holds and nobody answers. Built: the step reads `fails` with `objected: defeated`; its conclusion reads unsupported, never refuted. Options: (a) fails, as built — a defeated warrant is false, like a refuted claim, and a change walk reports the step "broken"; (b) unknown, like a contested step — the step only stops supporting, and "defeated" lives only in `objected`. Recommended: (a). It is wrong if a reader takes "fails" on a step to mean its premises are false.
properties.name: IDEA (proposed 2026-10-20, phase 6 PR 1): when an objection to a step is established and unanswered, does the step read "fails" (built) or "unknown"?
properties.rationale:
req:an-objection-aimed-at-a-step-is-read-against-that-step says "the step is defeated and does not support its conclusion"; both options meet it. (a) keeps the three-valued verdict telling defeated apart from contested; (b) keeps `fails` meaning a premise failed. The conclusion reads the same either way.
